description: Small table of per-character unique image asset-name lists. The export contains only CP_270 variants whose image slots are all None; no consumer of the table or its field was identifiable in the reconstructed source.

ID.simple: Row key, apparently a character/variation ID (CP_270_00, CP_270_10).
ID.technical: FName primary key (ImportKeyField=Id in the export). CharacterVariationDataTable has an Id_CharacterUniqueImage FName field, but no reconstructed code reads that field, and CharacterUniqueImageDataTable is not one of the table names registered/loaded by AGameDataTableManager::StartInitialLoading or resolved in its Tick. The lookup key can therefore be described only as a serialized row key, not as an observed join.

ImageFileName.simple: Array of unique image asset names for the row (all None in the export).
ImageFileName.technical: TArray<FName> with 16 slots in both exported rows, all NAME_None. The field is a serialized property of FGameDataTableRow_CharacterUniqueImage (retail row struct 0x16cc740 with a verified layout pin), but no substantive consumer was found in Source/ or Plugins/: ImageFileName appears only in the row struct declaration/constructor. No behavior, loader type or UI use can be attributed to it from the available evidence.

notes: Export contains exactly 2 rows (CP_270_00 and CP_270_10); both have 16 ImageFileName entries and every entry is None, so the table conveys no active asset references in the available data.

Limit: the only identifier-level connection is CharacterVariation::Id_CharacterUniqueImage, which is itself unread in the reconstructed source. The table is not loaded by the reconstructed DataTable manager path (no loader name and no manager array), so this documentation deliberately stops at serialization/loader-level observations rather than inventing a consumer.
No per-locale or numbered-shard variants exist in the export. Retail may use this table through code not represented in the reconstruction or through Blueprint; that cannot be established here.
The row struct layout is recorded in Tools/verify layout checks (offset 0x8 Id, 0x10 ImageFileName), but that is reconstruction evidence, not a consumer.

usages.detail: Only identifier-level link: a CharacterVariation row has an Id_CharacterUniqueImage FName, with no reconstructed reader.
Declares the serialized ImageFileName array; no consumer found.
Records the retail row-struct address and construct thunk for the type, establishing that the struct exists in retail.
